title: Cap. IX Arg. 11 (Corvinus): absolute predestination/reprobation makes baptism of many infants, by God's first intention, useless and sealing nothing — without the infants' fault
pass_a_gloss: They who place predestination and reprobation as depending absolutely from the freest will of God, and not from the foreseen faith and unbelief of the predestined and reprobate, those make Baptism administered about many infants to be established as useless from the first intention of God, and to seal nothing, and that without the fault of the infants unto whom it is administered. For if we place many infants of the faithful as precisely reprobated, it is most certain that nothing is sealed unto them by Baptism.
pass_b_english: Those who set predestination and reprobation as hanging absolutely on God's freest will — not on foreseen faith and unbelief of the predestined and reprobate — make baptism administered to many infants useless by God's first intention, and sealing nothing, and that without fault in the infants who receive it. For if we set many infants of the faithful as precisely reprobated, it is most certain that baptism seals nothing for them.
source_text: Qui ponunt praedestinationem et reprobationem ex liberrima Dei voluntate absolute pendentem, et non ex praevisa fide et infidelitate praedestinatorum et reprobatorum, illi faciunt Baptismum circa multos infantes administratum, ex prima Dei intentione statui inutilem, et nihil obsignare, idque citra culpam infantium quibus administratur. Nam si ponamus multos infantes fidelium praecise reprobatos, nihil ipsis per Baptismum obsignari certissimum est.
